A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same XOXO/GCGS work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive rewriting and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original attack experiments, a GitHub Copilot demonstration, an assistant survey and supplementary analyses, including adversarial fine-tuning and cross-model warm-up.

after.justification: v4 retains original attack experiments and the Copilot demonstration, and reports additional confidence-monotonicity and sampling-temperature results.

M1.justification: The documented generation-search score changes from summed token log probabilities in v2 Appendix A to length-normalized log likelihood in v4 Equation 1 and Appendix A.1, potentially changing transformation rankings. The two-phase search, identifier replacements and warm-up remain. Identical retained results do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: HumanEval+, MBPP+, CWEval/Python, Devign defect detection, BigCloneBench clone detection and the CodeSearchNet identifier source remain. The Copilot demonstration and seven-assistant survey also remain. Moving classification experiments into v4 Appendix B.3 and changing decoding temperature do not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Main comparator membership is unchanged: generation variants GCGS/GCGS+P become XOXO/+GCGS, while ALERT, MHM, RNNS and WIR-Random remain in classification comparisons. However, v2 Appendix F's standalone attack-level comparison against GCGS without combinations is no longer reported; v4 instead compares individual and composed transformation confidence scores.

E3.justification: Primary dataset splits, model configurations, three-example prompts and temperature-zero evaluations remain. v4 adds a temperature-1.0 evaluation of Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B across three retained benchmarks. Its monotonicity evaluation compares sampled transformation pairs with their compositions, replacing v2's attack-success/query-efficiency comparison.

E4.justification: Supporting analyses change substantially. v4 adds temperature sensitivity and direct testing of confidence under transformation composition, while dropping v2's cross-model warm-up analysis, zero-shot classifier-selection diagnostic and Appendix F's aggregate composition-ablation findings. The subtle-bug analysis, vulnerability case studies and adversarial fine-tuning experiments are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix F states hypothesis rejection without identifying a statistical test or reporting p-values. v4 Section 4.2 specifies a one-tailed t-test, its comparison and alternative hypothesis, and p-values below 1.7 × 10^-10. Main five-seed reporting and the closed-model single-full-run plus five-small-run practice remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched main attack, naturalness, fine-tuning and variance tables retain their numbers. Supplementary results change substantially: v4 Table 5 newly reports temperature-1.0 Qwen 32B ASRs of 99.56%, 97.50% and 82.54% on HumanEval+, MBPP+ and CWEval, respectively. These are different-setting results, not same-setting gains. New assistant sampling measurements appear in Table 17; v2's cross-model warm-up results, zero-shot accuracy rows and aggregate composition-ablation results disappear.

T1.justification: v4 revises the confidence function's codomain from [0,1] to real values and explicitly defines length-normalized generation log likelihood, unlike v2's summed score. It also qualifies the free-group tree as an abstraction over transformation sequences with validity constraints, replacing unrestricted-composition wording. No theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central XOXO, GCGS and Copilot claims remain. Headline scope narrows from v2's 75.72% average across five tasks and eleven models to v4's 73.20% across generation attacks on eight models; classification evidence remains in the appendix. v4 additionally foregrounds discovery of confidence monotonicity as a contribution and explicitly frames the findings as an LLM architectural limitation.

C2.justification: v4 newly synthesizes the retained vulnerability cases as failures through omitted defensive checks and connects this interpretation to guarding limitations. It argues that minimal context and temperature-zero evaluation conservatively bound real-world attacks. Expanded limitations identify function-level Python scope, assistant-specific adaptation and imperfect context transferability, while v2's explicit warning that monotonicity may fail across architectures is removed.

D1.justification: v4 supplies an explicit repository address, whereas v2's checklist only asserts that code is available. It adds recovered assistant sampling parameters and expands dataset-license information, including revising the reported CodeXGLUE license. Algorithm 1 also resolves inconsistencies in transformed-input scoring, identity initialization and composition; collision avoidance was already documented in v2 Appendix A.

R1.justification: v4 substantially repositions the work around jailbreak distinctions, surrogate-free generation attacks and confidence-guided search. It adds discussion of CodeAttack, AutoDAN-family attacks and confidence literature, plus supply-chain and insider-threat references supporting the threat model. This replaces much of v2's broader non-adversarial robustness and large-context background framing.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, threat-model explanation, method exposition and evaluation narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves forward; architecture, threat model and demonstration are grouped; classification and warm-up move into the appendix; defenses gain a main-text section. Ethical Considerations replaces the short broader-impact treatment, and the NeurIPS checklist is removed.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a two-column layout, redraws and reorders the attack overview and Copilot workflow figures, and relocates the subtle-bug chart and example into the main text. Tables and code listings are extensively reformatted. Temperature and assistant-parameter tables are added, while cross-model warm-up tables and the zero-shot accuracy panel are removed.

improvement.justification: v4 makes GCGS more internally consistent through corrected pseudocode and explicit confidence definitions, improves the explanatory figures, and states practical applicability limits more clearly. New mechanism and temperature analyses add useful evidence. The gains are limited by removal of transferability evidence and by real-world lower-bound claims that the one-model temperature study does not establish.
